days.title: First Day: Read the Introduction Lesson Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: What stands out to you in the notes regarding Paul's letter to the believers in Rome?
How did the lecture challenge or encourage you as you embark on your study of Romans?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 1:1-7.
days.summary: God called Paul to present the gospel to Roman believers.

subquestions.text: How did Paul describe himself to the believers in Rome?
What additional information about Paul do you find in Acts 9:20-22 and 1 Timothy 1:12-16?
The word "gospel" means "good news." What good news is proclaimed in these verses, and why is it good?
How have you experienced this good news?
In what ways did Paul encourage and uphold the Christians in Rome?
How might this encouragement impact your interactions with other believers?

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 1:8-10.
days.summary: Paul thanked God for the believers in Rome.

questions.text: Why was Paul thankful for the believers in Rome?

subquestions.text: What did Paul pray for specifically, and how did God answer his prayer? (See also Acts 21:33-34; 22:25-29; 28:14-16.)
What do these verses teach about the relationship between serving God and prayer?

questions.text: How do Paul's prayers encourage you to pray, and for whom or what will you pray?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 1:11-15.
days.summary: Paul longed to visit the believers in Rome.

questions.text: Why did Paul want to visit Rome, and what might have kept him away?
How might Paul's experience offer encouragement when you encounter obstacles when serving God? (See also Acts 28:11-16.)

subquestions.text: Describe Paul's obligation to all people and his attitude toward his obligation. (See also Acts 26:11-20.)
How does the call to share your knowledge about Jesus with others impact your life?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 1:16-17.
days.summary: Paul emphatically stated the gospel's worth.

questions.text: Give reasons for Paul's unashamed confidence in the gospel of Christ.
In what situations might you find yourself tempted to be ashamed of the gospel? How do Paul's words strengthen or encourage you?

subquestions.text: How are verses 16 and 17 a part of Paul's personal testimony? (See also Philippians 3:4-9.)
Describe how verses 16 and 17 may relate to your experience of the gospel. What word or phrase stands out to you or is a part of your personal testimony?

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 1:1-17.
days.summary: God reveals His saving power for all people through the gospel. No homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders

questions.text: What power do you find in the gospel of Christ? How do the truths in this passage empower you to unashamedly share this good news with others?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 1 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: How did the lecture build your confidence in the power of the gospel of Jesus Christ?
From the notes, what good news about Jesus Christ stood out to you?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 1:18-20.
days.summary: God reveals His wrath against sinful people.

questions.text: Define "wrath" and explain why God is revealing His wrath.
Define "suppress" and explain why people might suppress the truth about God.

subquestions.text: What does the natural world reveal about God, and how is this meaningful to you?
What does the natural world not reveal about God, and where can these truths be discovered? (See also Matthew 5:14-16; John 1:4-9; 8:12; 2 Timothy 3:16; and any other verses you know.)

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 1:21-23.
days.summary: Humanity exchanged worship of God for idolatry.

questions.text: Describe humanity's response to God's revealed truth and the results of this response.
What "exchange" is described in verse 23? (See also verse 25.)
What substitutes for God do you worship or serve, and how might you come to recognize them?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 1:24-28.
days.summary: God gave humanity over to sexual sin.

subquestions.text: What phrase occurs three times to describe God's response to humanity's choice, and what stands out to you as you read the progression of the phrase?
How does this phrase help you understand God's wrath?

In what ways does Scripture help you understand Paul's link between the sin of idolatry and sexual immorality? (See also Genesis 1:26-27; 2:24-25; Isaiah 50:1; Jeremiah 3:1, 8; 1 Corinthians 6:9-11, 18-20; Ephesians 5:31-32; and any other verses you know.)
What lies about sin have replaced God's truth in your culture or in your life?

questions.text: Write a prayer for yourself or others you know who are living with the consequences of suppressing God's truth.

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 1:28-32.
days.summary: God gave people over to sin's depravity.

subquestions.text: Why did God give humanity over to a depraved mind?
How is a "depraved" mind different from one that does "not think it worthwhile to retain the knowledge of God"?

questions.text: What does approval of these sins look like in your culture and perhaps in your life? Why might sin receive approval?
How has God changed your thinking about a sin you previously approved and maybe even practiced?
With whom is God prompting you to share the good news of righteousness through faith in Jesus, and when might you do so?

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 1:18-32.
days.summary: Nothing is more important than how we respond to God. No homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders

questions.text: What do you learn from this passage about the results of humanity's rejection of God and His ways?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 2 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: How did the lecture challenge you regarding sin?
What teaching from the notes helped clarify your understanding about idolatry and accountability to God?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 2:1-4.
days.summary: Paul revealed shocking truth about God's judgment.

questions.text: What message does Paul clearly give his readers in verse 1?

subquestions.text: Explain the difference between God's judgment and that of a mere human.
What happens to those who judge others, and why?
In what ways do people wrongly judge others, and how are you prone to fall into this sin?
For what do we show contempt when we judge others? What truth about God and repentance do we miss?
How might God use you to extend His kindness and lead others to repentance?

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 2:5-16.
days.summary: God will bring judgment against all sinners.

questions.text: What traits do the people Paul describes possess? What do they store up for themselves?

subquestions.text: From verses 7-11, what are the two types of people Paul speaks of? What do they seek and what will they receive?
What do you seek, and what do your actions reveal about your heart attitude toward God?
As you ponder the truth that God shows no favoritism, what challenges or encourages you?

questions.text: Give details about how God's law impacts His judgment. When will this judgment take place?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 2:17-24.
days.summary: Paul questioned the religious superiority of the Jews.

subquestions.text: What led the Jews to wrongly see themselves as superior to others?
What privileges have you received from God, and what is your attitude toward those privileges?
Which commandments does Paul address in this passage, and why might he have mentioned these commands?
What happens when people violate the standards they proclaim?

questions.text: In what way might you excuse or justify sin in your own life?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 2:25-29.
days.summary: Paul defined true circumcision.

questions.text: Read Genesis 17:9-14. What did circumcision represent to the Jews, and why did Jewish people point to this rite with pride?
What outward signs do people seek or rely on today as evidence of a right relationship with God?
According to this passage, how did Paul describe a true Jew, and what does this mean to you?

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 2.
days.summary: God alone perfectly judges every person. No homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders

questions.text: What does the truth about God and His righteous judgment of sinners mean to you today?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 3 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: What points from the lecture stirred your thinking about humanity's inexcusable sin before God?
How did the notes speak to you in a new way regarding God's judgment of believers and unbelievers?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 3:1-4.
days.summary: Paul responded to objections about God's faithfulness.

subquestions.text: What advantages might Jews have claimed because they were entrusted with God's very words? (See also Romans 2:6-29.)
How does God's Word offer spiritual advantages? What other spiritual advantages do believers enjoy?

questions.text: How do God's promises to the Jews help you understand God's faithfulness mentioned in Romans 3:3-4? (See also Genesis 12:1-7; Deuteronomy 30:15-20; Jeremiah 31:35-37; and other verses you know.)

subquestions.text: From Psalm 51:1-6; John 3:18-19; and James 1:13-14, who is responsible for a person's sin and unbelief?
How does this truth impact your view of your own sin, and how can you pray for God's help?

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 3:5-8.
days.summary: Paul responded to objections about God's justice.

subquestions.text: What "human argument" did Paul expose as wrong?
Why is God's wrath justified? (See also Romans 1:18-32; 2:1-5.)
What does Paul's response to this human argument reveal about the people who believe it? (See also Luke 6:46.)
What human argument do you give for your sin? What does this reveal about your attitude toward sin, and how can you ask for help?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 3:9-18.
days.summary: Paul described humanity's sinful condition using Old Testament passages.

questions.text: Write down the attributes that immediately follow Paul's use of the term "no one" in verses 10-12. What does this say about the state of humanity?

subquestions.text: What words or phrases in verses 13-14 reveal how seriously God views our speech? (See also Psalms 14:1-3; 53:1-3.)
What warning do you receive about your own words? (See also James 3:5-10; Matthew 12:34-37.)
How would you like God to grow and change the heart motives behind your words and actions?
According to verse 18, what root sin underlies the sins in verses 13-17?
What does it look like to fear (have a reverent awe for) God?
From these verses, what do you learn about the powerful effects of sin?
How have you seen sin's effects in your life?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 3:19-20.
days.summary: Paul concluded his thoughts on human unrighteousness.

questions.text: What did Paul conclude in verses 19-20?
What did Paul mean by "every mouth may be silenced and the whole world held accountable to God"?

subquestions.text: What excuses for specific sins have you been giving God, and why?
How do these verses impact your views on religious rule-following?

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 3:1-20.
days.summary: All people are condemned for their sin and accountable to God. No homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders

questions.text: How has the study of Romans so far helped you to identify, confess, and turn from your sin?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 4 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: How did the lecture impact your understanding of humanity's sinful condition?
How did the notes raise your awareness of God's grace toward you, a sinner?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 3:21-22.
days.summary: Righteousness from God has been made known.

subquestions.text: Define righteousness. According to these verses, where does righteousness come from, and how is it received?
What does "apart from the law" reveal about how people are tempted to pursue righteousness?

questions.text: How do the Old Testament law and prophets testify that the righteousness God gives is apart from the law? (See also Genesis 15:6; Jeremiah 31:33-34; Ezekiel 36:23-27; and any other Scriptures.)
What does God's willingness to give righteousness to all through faith in Jesus reveal about Him? (See also John 1:12; Romans 10:9-10.) How does this challenge or encourage you?

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 3:23-24.
days.summary: All people need the salvation God offers by grace through faith.

questions.text: Skim Paul's examples in Romans 3:9-18 of humanity falling short of God's glory. What additional examples can you give to explain this truth?

subquestions.text: Define what it means to be justified.
How is the justification of sinners accomplished? (See also Isaiah 53:10-11; Luke 18:14;
2 Corinthians 5:21; Galatians 2:16; Philippians 3:9; Romans 8:1; or other Scriptures.)
How does understanding this truth impact how you view your relationship with God?
How do Hosea 3:1-2; Ephesians 1:7-8; Titus 2:11-14; and 1 Peter 1:18-19 help you understand redemption through Christ Jesus?
Why is God's grace in justification and redemption good news? With whom would you like to share this news?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 3:25-26.
days.summary: Jesus's blood atones for humanity's sin.

subquestions.text: Skim Hebrews 10:1-18. What does Paul mean in Romans 3:25 when he says Jesus was a "sacrifice of atonement" (also translated as "propitiation")?
How does this assure you that God's justice has been satisfied? (See also John 19:30; Hebrews 2:17; 1 John 2:2; 4:10.)

questions.text: What does Jesus's role in redemption and atonement reveal about Him?
How can you express your gratitude for such great love?

days.title: Fifth Day: Reread Romans 3:25-26.
days.summary: God's justice has been satisfied.

questions.text: How did God treat the sins of those who had faith in Him before Christ's sacrifice of atonement? (See also Genesis 9:5-6; Deuteronomy 28; and any other Scripture references for help.)
How does God's saving work through Christ prove that God is just toward sin and willing to justify sinners? (See also Romans 6:23.)
How do the following verses deepen our understanding of God's justice and righteousness in salvation?

subquestions.text: Psalm 33:5
Psalm 89:14
Psalm 103:6
Isaiah 9:7
Isaiah 51:5

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 3:21-26.
days.summary: God has made the way to be declared right with Him. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 3:21-26

questions.text: How have you responded to God's provision of righteousness for you through faith in Jesus?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 5 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: What truth about salvation from the lecture struck you most, and why?
From the notes, what aspect of Paul's message contains good news for you or someone you love?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 3:27-28.
days.summary: Paul revealed faith's impact on pride.

subquestions.text: From verse 27, what is excluded? Why?
What impact does faith have on pride? Why?
When might we be tempted to boast about our spirituality or relationship with God?
What are some results of this type of boasting?

questions.text: In what situations are you tempted to justify yourself to God, and how can you guard against self-righteousness?

days.title: Third Day: Reread Romans 3:27-28.
days.summary: Paul declared faith's role in salvation.

subquestions.text: Describe characteristics of saving faith by which sinners are justified. (See also John 1:12; 3:14-18; 20:30-31; Ephesians 2:8-9; Romans 10:9; Hebrews 11; or other verses.)
How do people understand and use the word "faith" in your culture? How does this understanding compare with the biblical definition?

questions.text: Looking back to last week's lesson, explain in your own words why justification by faith apart from works is good news.
In what ways does your faith in Jesus impact your life choices and relationships?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 3:29-30.
days.summary: Paul affirmed there is one God and one path to justification.

questions.text: Who are Gentiles, and why would Jews in Paul's day look down on them? (See also Romans 2:17, 23, 25. Use a dictionary if necessary.)
How does the fact that "there is only one God" and one salvation compare with modern thoughts on spirituality?
What truths from Romans 3:21-30 could you share to respond graciously to people who see all religions as viable options or believe there are many gods or many ways to God?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 3:31.
days.summary: Paul asserted that justification by faith upholds God's law.

subquestions.text: In your own words, summarize what God's law requires. (See also Exodus 20:1-17; Romans 6:23; 13:8-10.)
What role does the law play in a person's ability to attain righteousness? (See also Romans 3:20; Galatians 3:24.)
How did Jesus fulfill the law? (See Romans 3:25-26; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 2:17; 4:15.)

questions.text: If God has justified you through faith, give examples of how He encourages and enables your loving obedience. (See also Romans 8:12-17, 31-34; Philippians 2:12-13; 1 John 1:5-10.)

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 3:27-31.
days.summary: God justifies people through faith in Christ alone. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 3:27-31

questions.text: What does God's plan to justify sinners through faith alone reveal about Him? How have you responded to His invitation to faith in Jesus as your Savior?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 6 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: How did the lecture help you understand that all people must come to Christ for salvation?
What truth from the notes did you find encouraging or challenging?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 4:1-5.
days.summary: Abraham's example demonstrates that God justifies the ungodly.

questions.text: Why does Paul say Abraham could not boast before God? (See also Romans 3:27.)

subquestions.text: What did Abraham believe? In what ways did he honor God? (See also Genesis 12:1-9; 15:1-6, 18; 17:1-10, 23.)
How does Paul say those who work for wages differ from those who trust God?

questions.text: What does your life reveal about your beliefs about God and reflect about your relationship with Him?

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 4:6-8.
days.summary: David's example demonstrates that God forgives and covers sin.

questions.text: Read 2 Samuel 11-12 and Psalms 32; 51. How did David learn the truth Paul quoted from Psalm 32?

subquestions.text: What do you learn from David's experience with God concerning his sin?
How can these verses help someone struggling with guilt from past or present sin?

questions.text: Spend time reflecting on your specific sins that God has counted against Christ. How will you thank Jesus for bearing your sins on the cross? Share with your group a time when you experienced the joy of God's forgiveness.

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 4:9-15.
days.summary: Righteousness comes by faith.

questions.text: Read Genesis 15:1-6; 17:10-14, 24-27; and Galatians 3:15-18. Why is this sequence of events important in regard to God's declaration of righteousness?

subquestions.text: What happens when a person depends on good behavior or outward religious observances as a measure of righteousness?
Explain the value of upright living, or following "in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had."

questions.text: Do you believe you are righteous in God's eyes? Why or why not?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 4:16-25.
days.summary: God made Abraham the father of all who believe.

questions.text: Who are Abraham's offspring, and how does God's guaranteed promise come to them?

subquestions.text: What do these verses say about Abraham's faith, and what stands out most to you?
What happened with Abraham's faith as he awaited the fulfillment of God's promise?

questions.text: What do the words "it was credited to him as righteousness" mean for believers today, and how does this truth impact you?
How has God worked through a hopeless situation to strengthen your faith?

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 4.
days.summary: God gives Christ's righteousness to those who believe in Him. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 4

questions.text: As you review Romans 4, pay special attention to the places that the terms "credited" and "blessed" are mentioned. What have you learned this week about the way God justifies His people, and what influence does this truth have on your life?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 7 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: What truths from the lecture helped clarify your understanding of God's justification of Abraham and all believers?
How did the notes encourage or challenge you as you consider Abraham's unwavering faith?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 5:1-2.
days.summary: Justification brings believers peace with God.

subquestions.text: Explain what peace with God means and how people receive this peace. (See also Romans 2:5; 4:5-7.)
How do peaceful circumstances or feelings compare to the peace a believer has with God?
From verse 2, what do believers receive through Jesus? Which words stand out to you, and why?
Read John 14:6; Ephesians 2:18; 3:12; and Hebrews 4:14-16. How do these verses describe the access believers enjoy, and how should this privilege impact your life?
Give practical ways to focus your hope on the glory of God.
How might the hope of God's glory offer you needed help today? (See also Psalm 17:15; Matthew 5:8; 1 John 3:2; Revelation 22:3-4; and other Bible passages you may know.)

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 5:3-5.
days.summary: Suffering produces fruit in the lives of believers.

subquestions.text: What fruit does suffering produce in God's people? What might each of these look like in a believer's life?
How might believers glory in suffering? (See also Romans 8:17; Philippians 4:4-7; and other Bible passages you may know.)
In what ways has God worked to produce fruit in your times of suffering?

questions.text: What is the hope that does "not put us to shame," and how has this helped you personally?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 5:6-8.
days.summary: God demonstrates His love for sinners through Christ's death.

questions.text: Give the words Paul used to describe those for whom Christ died, and explain why this is good news.

subquestions.text: How do these words help clarify the role people play in their salvation? (See also Ephesians 2:1-9.)
What is your experience of this truth?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 5:9-11.
days.summary: Christ's life and death offer salvation to sinners.

questions.text: List salvation's various aspects from these verses.

subquestions.text: Define "reconciliation." Is God reconciled to us, or are we reconciled to God?
What does God's gift of reconciliation reveal about Him?

questions.text: How do Christ's death and life save us, and what does it mean to boast in Him? (See also Romans 4:25; 6:8-10; 8:34; Hebrews 7:24-25; or other Bible passages you may know.)

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 5:1-11.
days.summary: Believers have peace with God and hope in all circumstances. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 5:1-11

questions.text: In what ways will you glory, rejoice, or boast in God for His gift of reconciliation with Him?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 8 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: How did the lecture help you better understand or apply a believer's peace with and reconciliation
What aspect of reconciliation given in the notes stood out to you and why?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 5:12-14.
days.summary: Sin and death entered the world through one man.

subquestions.text: Read Genesis 2:15-3:24. Who is the "one man" Paul spoke of in Romans 5:12?

From Genesis 2:15-3:24, what command and warning did God give the man, and what harm did his breaking of God's command cause? (See also Romans 3:9-11, 23; 8:20-21; 1 Corinthians 15:22; Ephesians 2:1-3.)

questions.text: How does verse 12 challenge the misconception that people are born good or morally neutral?

subquestions.text: Verses 13 and 14 reveal that death reigned before the law was given to Moses. What do these verses teach us about the relationship between sin and death?
Who is "the one to come" mentioned in verse 14, and why do we need Him? (See also Romans 5:15-21.)

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 5:15-19.
days.summary: Paul contrasted God's gift and Adam's trespass.

questions.text: List the different aspects of "the gift" and "the trespass." What do you learn about each?

subquestions.text: How are all people impacted by Adam's trespass, and how can they access God's gift through Christ? (See also John 3:7-21; Romans 10:9-13; or other Bible passages.)
Which reigns in your life: death from Adam or justification from Christ? How do you know?

days.title: Fourth Day: Reread Romans 5:15-19.
days.summary: Paul explained the consequences of the gift and the trespass.

questions.text: List ways Adam and Jesus are the same and how they differ. What stands out to you?
What do you learn about God's grace through His gift, and how does grace impact you?
Ponder the words "how much more." What do you think Paul meant? How would you describe what he meant to someone else?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 5:20-21.
days.summary: Adam brought sin, but by grace Jesus brought life.

questions.text: How does the law cause "the trespass" to increase, and how do you see this at work in your life? (See also Romans 5:13-14; 7:7-12; Galatians 3:24.)
What are the two "reigns" mentioned in verse 21? What happens to those in each kingdom? (See also Colossians 1:13-14.)
Share a recent example of how God's grace met you in your struggle with sin.

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 5:12-21.
days.summary: Christ's gift of righteousness triumphs over Adam's sin. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 5:12-21

questions.text: What are some ways that God spoke or revealed His amazing grace to you this week? How will you pray accordingly?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 9 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: What helpful perspective of God's grace did you receive from the lecture?
From the notes, how do a believer's union with Christ and peace with God impact daily life?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 6:1-4.
days.summary: Paul taught that believers no longer live in sin.

questions.text: What thoughts in chapter 5 prompted Paul to ask the question in 6:1, and why? (See also
Who are "we" and "us" in these verses? If you are part of this group, rewrite verse 2 to describe you.
From your experience, what happens when Christians believe their sin does not matter? (See also Romans 1-3.)
When have you allowed yourself to believe God's gracious forgiveness makes your sin excusable?

days.title: Third Day: Reread Romans 6:1-4.
days.summary: Paul used baptism to illustrate a believer's death to sin.

questions.text: Describe the spiritual reality to which water baptism points. (See also Matthew 28:19-20; Acts 1:5; 2:38; 1 Corinthians 12:13; Galatians 3:26-27; Colossians 2:11-12.)

subquestions.text: Specifically, how did Paul say believers have died to sin?
If Christ is your Savior, how have you experienced this death, and in what ways are you living a new life? (See also Romans 5:12-21; 2 Corinthians 5:14-21.)
What power strengthens believers to live a new life? How does this impact your view of sin?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 6:5-10.
days.summary: Believers are eternally united with Christ.

questions.text: From these verses, name ways believers are united with Christ.

subquestions.text: Romans 6:5
Romans 6:6-7
Romans 6:8-9
Romans 6:10

questions.text: How do Ephesians 4:22-24 and Colossians 3:5-10 help explain what Paul meant by "our old self"?
For which aspects of your union with Christ will you thank God, and where do you need His help to believe He has set you free from sin? (See also Colossians 2:11-15 or other verses you know.)

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 6:9-11.
days.summary: Believers should view themselves through their union with Christ.

subquestions.text: From verses 9-11, list facts about Jesus and those who believe in Him.
As you meditate on these facts about Jesus and His people, how do they impact your attitudes and beliefs? What do you learn and take to heart?

questions.text: What would it look like for you to be dead to sin but alive to Christ in each of the following?

subquestions.text: Your home
Your school, workplace, or community
Your church, service, or worship

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 6:1-11.
days.summary: A believer's new identity in Christ frees them from sin's power. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 6:1-11

questions.text: How does Paul's command for believers to consider themselves dead to sin challenge or encourage you? What truth will you pray to make a part of your life this week?

days.title: First Day: Read the Lesson 10 Notes.
days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

questions.text: What insights about salvation did you find meaningful in the lecture?
How did the notes impact your ability to explain a believer's death to sin and union with Christ?

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 6:12-14.
days.summary: Paul gave four commands and a promise.

questions.text: What truths in earlier chapters of Romans lead up to the word "therefore" in verse 12? (See Lesson 10 along with Romans 4:22-25; 5:17, 20-21; 6:3-11 and any other verses you find.)

subquestions.text: List the two negative and the two positive commands given in these verses, and explain why lasting change involves both negative and positive actions. (See also Ephesians 4:22-24; Colossians 3:9-10.)
In what ways are you tempted to offer any part of yourself to sin? How has union with Christ helped you to offer that aspect of yourself to Him instead?

questions.text: How does the promise in verse 14 make it possible to obey the commands in verses 12-13? (See also question 3.)

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 6:15-16.
days.summary: Paul explained why believers under grace should not sin.

days.title: Second Day: Read Romans 13:1.

questions.text: Define "be subject to" or "submit."

days.summary: Paul explained the consequence of refusal to submit to authority.

questions.text: When people refuse to submit to lawful authority, against whom do they actually rebel, and what consequences do they face?

subquestions.text: How can people be free from fear of those in authority?

questions.text: Write a prayer to God regarding your submission to authority or lack thereof.

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 13:5-7.
days.summary: Paul gave reasons for the Roman believers to submit to authority.

subquestions.text: What reasons did Paul give for submitting to authorities? What other reasons can you think of?
What do you think Paul meant by the phrase "a matter of conscience"?

Read Luke 20:22-25. What did Jesus say about paying taxes?
How do these instructions guide your attitude about paying taxes?

days.title: Fifth Day: Reread Romans 13:1-7.
days.summary: Paul exhorted believers to live rightly before God and others.

Exodus 20:12
Leviticus 19:32
1 Timothy 5:17
1 Timothy 6:15b-16
What are some specific ways you can show respect and honor to these people in your life?

questions.text: How is it possible to show honor and respect to someone whose decisions and character differ from yours?
How might your attitudes and actions set a God-honoring example as you respond to governing authorities?

days.title: Sixth Day: Review Romans 13:1-7.
days.summary: God sovereignly places people in positions of authority. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 13:1-7

days.summary: Paul explained the believer's debt of love.

Do you lean toward legal obedience or loving obedience? Why?

What helps you express love in challenging situations? (See also Matthew 5:44; John 13:34; 15:13; 1 Corinthians 8:1; Galatians 6:2; or any other verses that come to mind.)

days.title: Third Day: Read Romans 13:11.
days.summary: Paul called believers to wake up from slumber.

questions.text: How does the Bible describe or define this present time as the Lord's return draws close? (See also Matthew 4:17; Galatians 1:3-4.)
Why might Paul have reminded believers that salvation is nearer than when they first believed?

subquestions.text: List ways people slumber, and tell why believers need to wake up.
From what slumber might you need to awaken?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 13:12-13.
days.summary: Paul urged believers to step out of the darkness.

subquestions.text: What did Paul say to "put aside" and "put on" in verse 12? What does this mean? (See also 1 John 1:5-7.)
How does Jesus's light impact believers? (See also Matthew 5:16.)

questions.text: In what ways does your culture normalize behaviors that Paul declared indecent?
How might the lifestyle Paul encouraged serve as a challenge, warning, or victory in your life, and why?

days.title: Fifth Day: Read Romans 13:14.
days.summary: Paul told believers to clothe themselves in Christ.

questions.text: What do you think Paul meant by "clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ"? (See also Galatians 3:27; Ephesians 4:17-24.)
How does God "clothe" or enable believers to live for Him? (See also Galatians 5:22-23; Ephesians 6:10-18; Philippians 2:13.)
How might being clothed with Christ lead you to stop gratifying sinful desires and think more like God does?

days.summary: Jesus's promised return calls believers to live holy lives of love. Homiletics for Group and Administrative Leaders: Romans 13:8-14

How might you reflect these convictions in your life?

What will happen at God's judgment seat?

subquestions.text: When are you tempted to judge or look down on others regarding disputable matters?
How might your personal accountability to God help you stop judging others?

subquestions.text: How did Paul describe the kingdom of God?

days.summary: Paul pointed believers toward lives that promote peace and mutual edification.

How might overly zealous focus on disputable matters destroy the work of God? (See also Romans 12:1-8.)

questions.text: In verses 21-22, what did Paul conclude for stronger and weaker believers in disputable matters?
What personal preferences might the Lord be prompting you to set aside or keep to yourself for the good of others?

days.summary: The notes and lecture fortify the truth of the passage for understanding and application to daily life.

subquestions.text: How is Paul's description of pleasing one's neighbors different from how we might think about people-pleasing today?

questions.text: Describe situations in which you find it difficult to build others up or put them first.

What impact does Christian unity have on you, your church, or your relationships with other believers?

days.title: Fourth Day: Read Romans 15:7-12.

questions.text: What did Paul command the Romans to do, and why?
What did Jesus do on behalf of God's truth, and why is this important?

questions.text: How might Paul's words help when you struggle to find unity with other believers?

How did the lecture encourage or challenge you in a practical way this week?

days.summary: Paul commended the Roman believers.

subquestions.text: For what three things did Paul commend his readers?
How do Paul's commendations reflect his teaching and practical instructions in this letter?
In what ways has the teaching in the book of Romans brought similar fruit in your relationships with other believers and commitment to reach others with the gospel?

questions.text: How would you express the truths of the gospel to someone you know?

Why was this trip important?
